claims.text: The baseline TOR-TILD method uses an EAM reference potential and thermodynamic integration.
An MTP trained on TaVCrW DFT data can replace the EAM reference potential.
Free energy perturbation can replace thermodynamic integration for the solid–liquid Helmholtz free-energy calculation.
The MTP must reproduce the ab initio phase-space distributions of both the complex liquid and solid states.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution enables a valid FEP estimate.
FEP accuracy depends on overlap between the MTP-sampled reference distribution and the target ab initio distribution.
The MTP provides a computationally cheaper surrogate for DFT energies and forces during sampling.
Using FEP with the MTP bypasses the slow convergence associated with thermodynamic integration.
The proposed MTP+FEP method will reduce total computational time by more than 80% relative to TOR-TILD.
The MTP+FEP result will remain within 0.5 meV/atom of the TOR-TILD free-energy result.
Short-range order may occur in the solid phase of TaVCrW.
The solid-state SRO stabilization energy is approximately 2–3 meV/atom.
The supercell must be sufficiently large to capture the SRO stabilization energy without finite-size effects.
The temperature interval for validating the SRO contribution and electronic-excitation shifts must be 2000–2400 K.
Capturing SRO and relevant electronic features is necessary for the MTP to predict the melting free energy accurately.
The usual GGA-PBE/LDA underbinding and overbinding rules do not hold for V and Cr at 0 K.
Errors from the chosen GGA-PBE or LDA functional may propagate into the MTP training data.
Neglecting high-temperature magnetic fluctuations may introduce unquantified free-energy errors, particularly for Cr-rich compositions.
